Model Test 03.question: ১) (গাইড বই দেখে প্রথমেই কোন উত্তর ভুল ভাবার আগে একবার যথাযথ সুত্র থেকে দেখে নিবেন। আমরা প্রতি পরীক্ষার পরদিন ভুল থাকলে ঠিক করে দেই, তারপরও কোন ভুল আছে মনে হলে আমাদেরকে গ্রুপে বা পেজে জানাবেন। ধন্যবাদ।) Which lens is used for correction of myopia?
Model Test 03.exp:
In myopia (short-sightedness), parallel rays from distant objects are focused in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens diverges the incoming rays before they enter the eye, allowing the eye's optical system to focus the image on the retina.

  • Myopia → Concave lens

  • Hypermetropia → Convex lens

  • Astigmatism → Cylindrical lens

  • Toric lens → commonly used for astigmatism correction

High-yield Ophthalmology recall:
Myopia → concave (−) lens
Hypermetropia → convex (+) lens

Exam pearl:
“Myopia = minus power = concave lens.”

Model Test 03.question: ২) In which type of sock body temperature is usually raised?
Model Test 03.exp:
In septic shock, systemic infection triggers a strong inflammatory response with release of cytokines and other mediators, which commonly produces fever and raised body temperature. However, some patients—especially in severe sepsis—may develop hypothermia.

  • Septic shock → usually fever/raised temperature

  • Hypovolemic shock → usually normal or low temperature

  • Cardiogenic shock → usually cool, clammy skin and may have low temperature

  • Endocrine shock → temperature depends on the underlying disorder

High-yield Shock recall:
Septic shock → fever + warm peripheries may occur early due to vasodilation.
Later, severe septic shock can cause cold, clammy extremities.

Exam pearl:
“Shock + fever → think septic shock.”

Model Test 03.question: ৩) Which one is the most important cause of NGU?
৪) Which is the second line of immune defense?
Model Test 03.exp:
The body's defenses are commonly described in three lines:

  1. First line → Physical and chemical barriers: intact skin, mucous membranes, secretions, etc.

  2. Second line → Innate immunity: phagocytes, complement, inflammation, NK cells, fever, etc.

  3. Third line → Adaptive immunity: humoral and cell-mediated immunity.

Therefore, innate immunity is the second line of defense.

High-yield Immunology recall:
1st line → Skin & mucous membrane
2nd line → Innate immunity
3rd line → Adaptive immunity

Exam pearl:
“Barrier first, innate second, adaptive third.”

Model Test 03.question: ৫) Which excretory product is end product of nucleic acid metabolism?
Model Test 03.exp:
Uric acid is the major end product of purine (nucleic acid) metabolism in humans. Purine bases such as adenine and guanine are degraded through hypoxanthine and xanthine to uric acid, mainly via xanthine oxidase.

  • Uric acid → purine/nucleic acid metabolism

  • Urea → amino acid/protein metabolism

  • Creatinine → creatine/phosphocreatine metabolism in muscle

  • Bilirubin → hemoglobin/heme breakdown

High-yield Metabolism recall:
Purines → uric acid
Proteins/amino acids → urea
Creatine → creatinine
Heme → bilirubin

Exam pearl:
“Purine breakdown ends in uric acid.”

Model Test 03.question: ৬) Which of the following indicates active viral replication of HBV?
Model Test 03.exp:
HBeAg (hepatitis B e antigen) is a marker of active HBV replication and generally indicates high viral load and increased infectivity.

  • HBsAg → current HBV infection

  • HBeAg → active viral replication + high infectivity

  • Anti-HBc → previous or current exposure to HBV

  • HBcAg → not detectable in serum; found within infected hepatocytes

High-yield HBV recall:
HBeAg → active replication → high infectivity
Anti-HBe → generally indicates reduced replication/infectivity

Exam pearl:
“e = actively replicating HBV.”

Model Test 03.question: ৭) Which viral disease has cent percent mortality?
Model Test 03.exp:
Rabies is considered almost invariably fatal once clinical symptoms develop, with survival being exceptionally rare. The rabies virus causes progressive encephalitis, and once the symptomatic phase begins, there is no reliably effective curative treatment.

However, rabies is preventable with appropriate post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) before symptoms develop.

  • Rabies → nearly 100% fatal once clinical symptoms appear

  • Dengue → variable mortality

  • Herpes → usually not fatal

  • Polio → mortality occurs in a minority of paralytic cases

High-yield Virology recall:
Rabies → fatal after onset of clinical disease, but preventable with timely PEP.

Exam pearl:
“Rabies: almost 100% fatal after symptom onset.”

Model Test 03.question: ৮) Gradual loss of hearing in old age is called....?
Model Test 03.exp:
Presbycusis is the gradual, progressive sensorineural hearing loss associated with aging. It usually affects high-frequency sounds first and is typically bilateral and symmetrical.

  • Presbycusis → age-related sensorineural hearing loss

  • Presbyopia → age-related loss of near vision

  • Conductive deafness → external or middle ear pathology

  • Neural deafness → auditory nerve/central pathway pathology

High-yield Audiology recall:
Presbycusis = age + progressive + bilateral sensorineural hearing loss.

Exam pearl:
“Old age hearing loss = Presbycusis; old age near-vision loss = Presbyopia.”

Model Test 03.question: ৯) Which enzyme is not present in saliva?
Model Test 03.exp:
Saliva contains several enzymes, including salivary amylase, lingual lipase, and carbonic anhydrase. However, proteinase (proteolytic enzyme) is not a normal constituent of saliva.

  • Amylase → carbohydrate digestion

  • Lingual lipase → fat digestion

  • Carbonic anhydrase → contributes to bicarbonate secretion and oral pH regulation

  • Proteinase → not normally present as a salivary digestive enzyme

High-yield Saliva recall:
Saliva contains → Amylase + Lingual lipase + Carbonic anhydrase
No significant protein digestion occurs in the mouth.

Exam pearl:
“Saliva digests carbohydrate and some fat—not protein.”

Model Test 03.question: ১০) Brush-bordered cells are present in which part of renal tubule?
Model Test 03.exp:
Brush-bordered cells are characteristic of the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT). They have numerous microvilli on their apical surface, forming a prominent brush border that greatly increases the surface area for reabsorption.

The PCT is responsible for reabsorbing approximately 65–70% of filtered Na⁺ and water, along with most of the filtered glucose, amino acids, and bicarbonate.

  • PCT → prominent brush border

  • DCT → few/no microvilli, no prominent brush border

  • Thin limbs of loop of Henle → no brush border

High-yield Renal histology recall:
PCT → cuboidal cells + prominent brush border + abundant mitochondria.
DCT → cuboidal cells + no prominent brush border.

Exam pearl:
“Brush border = PCT.”

Model Test 03.question: ১১) Which parasitic disease occurs in urogenital tract?
Model Test 03.exp:
Trichomoniasis is a sexually transmitted parasitic infection caused by Trichomonas vaginalis, a flagellated protozoan that primarily infects the urogenital tract.

  • Trichomoniasis → urogenital tract

  • Amebiasis → intestine/liver

  • Giardiasis → small intestine

  • Cryptosporidiosis → gastrointestinal tract

High-yield Parasitology recall:
Trichomonas vaginalis → urogenital tract → sexually transmitted infection (STI).

Exam pearl:
“Urogenital protozoan = Trichomonas vaginalis.”

Model Test 03.question: ১২) Macula densa plays an important role in which renal autoregulatory mechanism?
Model Test 03.exp:
The macula densa is a specialized group of cells in the distal tubule that senses tubular NaCl concentration. It plays a central role in tubuloglomerular feedback (TGF), an important mechanism of renal autoregulation.

When NaCl delivery to the macula densa increases, it signals the afferent arteriole to constrict, reducing renal blood flow and GFR toward normal.

  • Macula densa → Tubuloglomerular feedback

  • Myogenic response → vascular smooth muscle responds to stretch

  • TGF → stabilizes renal blood flow and GFR

High-yield Renal physiology recall:
Macula densa senses NaCl → TGF → adjusts afferent arteriolar tone → regulates GFR.

Exam pearl:
“Macula densa = Tubuloglomerular feedback.”

Model Test 03.question: ১৩) Uncontrolled flow of saliva outside the mouth is called....?
Model Test 03.exp:
Drooling (sialorrhea) is the unintentional or uncontrolled flow of saliva outside the mouth. It may occur due to excessive salivation or, more commonly, impaired swallowing/oral motor control.

  • Drooling/Sialorrhea → uncontrolled salivary flow

  • Xerostomia → dry mouth due to reduced saliva

  • Sjögren syndrome → autoimmune disorder causing dry eyes and dry mouth

  • Aptyalism → absence or marked deficiency of salivary secretion

High-yield Salivary disorders recall:
Drooling = excessive/uncontrolled saliva
Xerostomia = dry mouth
Aptyalism = absent/reduced salivation

Exam pearl:
“Saliva flowing out uncontrollably = Drooling (sialorrhea).”

Model Test 03.question: ১৪) Which disease is common in cities like dhaka?
Model Test 03.exp:
Dengue is particularly common in urban and densely populated areas, including cities such as Dhaka, because Aedes aegypti thrives around human habitation and breeds in artificial containers holding stagnant water.

  • Dengue → urban areas → Aedes aegypti

  • Malaria → more common in rural/forest-endemic areas

  • Kala-azar → rural areas, especially endemic regions

  • Rabies → associated mainly with animal exposure, not specifically urban settings

High-yield Epidemiology recall:
Aedes aegypti → urban mosquito → dengue.

Exam pearl:
“Densely populated city + stagnant water containers = Dengue.”

Model Test 03.question: ১৫) Countercurrent exchanger formed by...?
Model Test 03.exp:
The vasa recta acts as the countercurrent exchanger in the kidney. It preserves the medullary osmotic gradient established by the countercurrent multiplier system of the loop of Henle, thereby helping maintain the kidney's ability to concentrate urine.

  • Loop of Henle → countercurrent multiplier

  • Vasa recta → countercurrent exchanger

  • PCT → bulk reabsorption

  • DCT → fine regulation of electrolytes

High-yield Renal physiology recall:
Loop of Henle = multiplier
Vasa recta = exchanger

Exam pearl:
“Multiplier = Loop; Exchanger = Vasa recta.”

Model Test 03.question: ১৬) Sterilization of heat sensitive material can be achieved by.......?
Model Test 03.exp:
Ethylene oxide (EtO) gas is used for sterilizing heat-sensitive and moisture-sensitive materials, such as plastic medical equipment, catheters, and electronic devices. It sterilizes by alkylating proteins and nucleic acids of microorganisms.

  • Autoclaving → moist heat; unsuitable for heat-sensitive materials

  • Boiling → disinfection, not reliable sterilization

  • Ethylene oxide → heat- and moisture-sensitive materials

  • Hot air oven → dry heat; requires high temperature

High-yield Sterilization recall:
Heat-sensitive materials → Ethylene oxide gas
Moist heat → Autoclave
Dry heat → Hot air oven

Exam pearl:
“Heat-sensitive = Ethylene oxide.”

Model Test 03.question: ১৭) Which is not a hormone of anterior pituitary?
Model Test 03.exp:
ADH (vasopressin) is not produced by the anterior pituitary. It is synthesized in the hypothalamus (mainly the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei) and stored/released from the posterior pituitary.

The anterior pituitary secretes several major hormones, including:

  • GH → Growth hormone

  • TSH → Thyroid-stimulating hormone

  • FSH → Follicle-stimulating hormone

  • ACTH, LH, and prolactin

High-yield Pituitary recall:
Anterior pituitary → “FLAT PiG”
FSH, LH, ACTH, TSH, Prolactin, GH

Exam pearl:
“ADH = hypothalamus-made, posterior pituitary-released.”

Model Test 03.question: ১৮) Which is responsible for regulation of secretory functions of GI tract?
Model Test 03.exp:
The Meissner (submucosal) plexus primarily regulates the secretory functions of the gastrointestinal tract and also influences local blood flow.

  • Meissner plexus → secretion + local blood flow

  • Auerbach/Myenteric plexus → GI motility

  • Pacinian plexus → not a component of the enteric nervous system

High-yield GI physiology recall:
Meissner = Secretion
Auerbach = Activity (motility)

Exam pearl:
“Meissner controls secretion; Auerbach controls movement.”

Model Test 03.question: ১৯) Streptococcus pneumoniae are chiefly found in.....?
Model Test 03.exp:
Streptococcus pneumoniae commonly colonizes the nasopharynx of healthy individuals, particularly children. From there, it can spread to adjacent sites or invade sterile tissues, causing diseases such as otitis media, sinusitis, pneumonia, meningitis, and bacteremia.

  • Nasopharynx → principal colonization site

  • Oropharynx → not the chief site

  • Skin → not a normal colonization site

  • Colon → not a normal colonization site

High-yield Microbiology recall:
S. pneumoniae → nasopharyngeal colonization → respiratory spread/invasive disease.

Exam pearl:
“Pneumococcus lives in the nasopharynx.”

Model Test 03.question: ২০) Which is the commonest organism for acute osteomyelitis?
Model Test 03.exp:
Staphylococcus aureus is the most common cause of acute osteomyelitis across most age groups. It can reach bone through hematogenous spread, direct inoculation, or contiguous spread.

  • S. aureus → commonest cause of acute osteomyelitis

  • S. epidermidis → prosthetic/device-associated infections

  • S. saprophyticus → urinary tract infections

  • M. tuberculosis → chronic tuberculous osteomyelitis

High-yield Osteomyelitis recall:
S. aureus → commonest overall
Sickle cell disease → Salmonella is classically associated
Puncture wound through shoe → Pseudomonas

Exam pearl:
“Acute osteomyelitis = S. aureus until proven otherwise.”

Model Test 03.question: ২১) which hormone is secreted from adrenal medulla?
Model Test 03.exp:
The adrenal medulla is derived from neural crest cells and secretes catecholamines. Its principal secretions are epinephrine and norepinephrine, with a small amount of dopamine also produced.

  • Adrenal medulla → Epinephrine, norepinephrine, dopamine

  • Cortisol → Adrenal cortex (zona fasciculata)

  • Aldosterone → Adrenal cortex (zona glomerulosa)

  • Androgens → Adrenal cortex (zona reticularis)

High-yield Adrenal gland recall:
Medulla → Catecholamines
Cortex → “GFR”

  • Glomerulosa → Aldosterone

  • Fasciculata → Cortisol

  • Reticularis → Androgens

Exam pearl:
“Adrenal medulla = catecholamines; cortex = steroid hormones.”

Model Test 03.question: ২২) Which of the following is a criteria of innate immunity?
Model Test 03.exp:
Innate immunity provides a rapid, non-specific defense against pathogens and begins acting within minutes to hours of exposure.

  • Acts within minutes → Innate immunity

  • Highly specific → Adaptive immunity

  • Improves after exposure → Adaptive immunity

  • Has immunological memory → Adaptive immunity

High-yield Immunology recall:
Innate immunity → rapid + non-specific + no immunological memory
Adaptive immunity → specific + slower initially + memory

Exam pearl:
“Innate = immediate; Adaptive = specific and remembers.”

Model Test 03.question: ২৩) All of the hormones are secreted by placenta except....?
Model Test 03.exp:
The placenta produces several important hormones, including hCG, estrogen, and progesterone. Prostaglandins are produced in reproductive tissues, including the decidua and fetal membranes, but are not classically considered placental hormones in standard MBBS physiology.

  • hCG → placental hormone

  • Estrogen → placental hormone

  • Progesterone → placental hormone

  • Prostaglandin → not classically a placental hormone

High-yield Placental hormones recall:
Major placental hormones: hCG, hPL, progesterone, and estrogens.

Exam pearl:
“Placenta: hCG + hPL + estrogen + progesterone.”

Model Test 03.question: ২৪) Enterochromaffin like (ECL) cells of stomach secrets....?
Model Test 03.exp:
Enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cells in the gastric mucosa secrete histamine, which stimulates parietal cells via H₂ receptors to increase HCl secretion.

  • ECL cells → Histamine

  • Parietal cells → HCl + intrinsic factor

  • Chief cells → Pepsinogen

  • G cells → Gastrin

  • Enterochromaffin (EC) cells → Serotonin

High-yield Gastric physiology recall:
G cell → Gastrin
ECL cell → Histamine
Parietal cell → HCl + intrinsic factor
Chief cell → Pepsinogen

Exam pearl:
“ECL → Histamine → H₂ receptor → HCl secretion.”

Model Test 03.question: ২৫) Fever with coated tongue & relative bradycardia in a patient mostly signifies.....?
Model Test 03.exp:
Typhoid fever classically presents with high-grade fever, coated tongue, and relative bradycardia (Faget sign). The relative bradycardia means the pulse rate is lower than expected for the degree of fever.

  • Typhoid → fever + coated tongue + relative bradycardia

  • TB → prolonged fever, weight loss, night sweats

  • Dengue → high fever, myalgia, headache, thrombocytopenia

  • Herpes → vesicular lesions and localized/systemic manifestations depending on type

High-yield Typhoid recall:
Salmonella Typhi → coated tongue + relative bradycardia (classical exam finding).

Exam pearl:
“Fever + coated tongue + relative bradycardia = Typhoid.”

Model Test 03.question: ২৬) Which hormone is a steroid in nature?
Model Test 03.exp:
Testosterone is a steroid hormone derived from cholesterol and synthesized mainly by the Leydig cells of the testes. Steroid hormones are generally lipid-soluble and act through intracellular/nuclear receptors.

  • Testosterone → steroid hormone

  • Oxytocin → peptide hormone

  • ADH → peptide hormone

  • Thyroxine (T4) → amine-derived hormone, although it is lipid-soluble

High-yield Endocrinology recall:
Steroid hormones → cortisol, aldosterone, testosterone, estrogen, progesterone.
Peptide hormones → insulin, ADH, oxytocin, GH.

Exam pearl:
“Cholesterol-derived hormones are steroids: testosterone, estrogen, progesterone, cortisol, aldosterone.”

Model Test 03.question: ২৭) The most commonly used filter is composed of.....?
Model Test 03.exp:
Nitrocellulose membrane filters are among the most commonly used membrane filters in microbiology and laboratory work. They are used for filtration of solutions that cannot be sterilized by heat, allowing microorganisms to be retained on the membrane.

  • Nitrocellulose → common membrane filter material

  • Nitroglycerin → explosive/vasodilator compound, not a filter material

  • Vinyl alcohol → not the standard answer

  • Monosodium tartrate → chemical compound, not a filter material

High-yield Microbiology recall:
Membrane filtration → nitrocellulose or cellulose acetate membranes
Used for heat-sensitive fluids.

Exam pearl:
“Common membrane filter material = Nitrocellulose.”

Model Test 03.question: ২৮) Factors Inhibiting the Secretion of Hydrochloric Acid excludes.....?
Model Test 03.exp:
Gastrin stimulates hydrochloric acid (HCl) secretion by acting directly on parietal cells and indirectly through ECL cells → histamine → H₂ receptors. Therefore, it is the factor that does not inhibit HCl secretion.

The other options inhibit gastric acid secretion:

  • Gastrin → stimulates HCl secretion

  • Secretin → inhibits gastric acid secretion

  • GIP → inhibits gastric acid secretion

  • Peptide YY (PYY) → inhibits gastric secretion and motility

High-yield Gastric physiology recall:
Stimulators of HCl → Gastrin + Histamine + ACh
Inhibitors → Somatostatin + Secretin + GIP + PYY

Exam pearl:
“Gastrin = acid ON; Somatostatin/Secretin/GIP = acid OFF.”

Model Test 03.question: ২৯) Sella turcica is the house of which endocrine gland?
Model Test 03.exp:
The sella turcica is a saddle-shaped depression in the sphenoid bone that contains the pituitary gland (hypophysis), specifically within its central depression called the hypophyseal fossa.

High-yield Anatomy recall:
Sella turcica → Pituitary gland
It is located in the middle cranial fossa.

Exam pearl:
“Sella turcica = seat of the pituitary gland.”

Model Test 03.question: ৩০) How natural killer cells gives innate immunity?
Model Test 03.exp:
Natural killer (NK) cells provide innate immunity primarily by recognizing and killing virus-infected cells and tumor cells, especially cells with reduced MHC class I expression. They kill target cells mainly through perforin and granzymes.

  • NK cells → kill virus-infected cells

  • Ingestion & destruction of microbes → phagocytes

  • Inhibiting viral replication → mainly interferon-mediated

  • Limiting spread of microbes → various innate mechanisms

High-yield Immunology recall:
NK cells → innate cytotoxicity → perforin + granzymes → apoptosis of infected cells.

Exam pearl:
“NK = Natural killers of virus-infected and tumor cells.”

Model Test 03.question: ৩১) Which enzyme is absent in pancreatic secretion?
Model Test 03.exp:
Pepsin is a gastric proteolytic enzyme produced by the chief cells of the stomach as pepsinogen. It is not present in pancreatic secretion.

Pancreatic juice contains:

  • Amylase → carbohydrate digestion

  • Lipase → fat digestion

  • Trypsinogen → activated to trypsin for protein digestion

  • Other proteolytic enzymes such as chymotrypsinogen and procarboxypeptidases

High-yield Pancreatic secretion recall:
Pancreas → Amylase + Lipase + Proteases
Stomach → Pepsin

Exam pearl:
“Pepsin = stomach; Trypsin = pancreas.”

Model Test 03.question: ৩২) Parathormone increases the absorption of phosphate from GI tract through........?
Model Test 03.exp:
Parathyroid hormone (PTH) increases renal 1α-hydroxylase activity, which converts vitamin D to its active form, calcitriol (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D). Calcitriol then increases intestinal absorption of both calcium and phosphate.

So, PTH increases phosphate absorption from the GI tract indirectly through calcitriol.

  • PTH → ↑ 1α-hydroxylase → ↑ Calcitriol → ↑ intestinal phosphate absorption

  • PTH also decreases renal phosphate reabsorption, causing phosphaturia.

High-yield Calcium–phosphate recall:
PTH → ↑ Ca²⁺, ↓ phosphate in blood
Calcitriol → ↑ intestinal absorption of Ca²⁺ + phosphate

Exam pearl:
“PTH raises intestinal phosphate absorption indirectly via calcitriol, but lowers serum phosphate by renal wasting.”

Model Test 03.question: ৩৩) Killing of many but not all microorganism is called....?
Model Test 03.exp:
Disinfection is the process of eliminating many or most pathogenic microorganisms from inanimate objects, but it does not necessarily destroy all microorganisms or bacterial spores.

  • Sterilization → destroys/removes all forms of microbial life, including spores

  • Disinfection → destroys many pathogens, but not necessarily spores

  • Antisepsis → destruction/inhibition of microorganisms on living tissues

  • Autoclaving → a method of sterilization using moist heat under pressure

High-yield Microbiology recall:
Sterilization = all microorganisms
Disinfection = most pathogens
Antisepsis = living tissue

Exam pearl:
“Disinfection kills many; sterilization kills all.”

Model Test 03.question: ৩৪) The definitive diagnosis of HIV can be done by which analysis method?
Model Test 03.exp:
In the classic HIV diagnostic algorithm, ELISA is used as an initial screening test, while Western blot was traditionally used as a confirmatory test for HIV infection by detecting antibodies against specific HIV proteins.

  • ELISA → screening

  • Western blot → traditional confirmatory test

  • RIA → not the standard HIV confirmatory test

  • Southern blot → DNA analysis, not HIV antibody diagnosis

High-yield HIV diagnosis recall:
Classic exam sequence → ELISA screening → Western blot confirmation.

Exam pearl:
“ELISA screens; Western blot confirms” — this is the classic textbook answer.

Note: Modern HIV diagnosis uses laboratory antigen/antibody immunoassays followed by differentiation assays and, when indicated, nucleic-acid testing rather than Western blot.

Model Test 03.question: ৩৫) Which one inhibits bone mineralisation?
Model Test 03.exp:
Cortisol inhibits bone formation and mineralisation when present in excess. It decreases osteoblast activity and reduces intestinal calcium absorption, contributing to osteoporosis with chronic glucocorticoid excess.

  • Cortisol → inhibits osteoblast activity and bone formation/mineralisation

  • Calcitonin → inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption

  • Insulin → promotes bone formation

  • Vitamin D → promotes calcium/phosphate absorption and supports bone mineralisation

High-yield Bone metabolism recall:
Cortisol excess → ↓ osteoblast activity → ↓ bone formation → osteoporosis
Vitamin D → ↑ Ca²⁺/phosphate absorption → mineralisation

Exam pearl:
“Excess cortisol = weak bones.”

Model Test 03.question: ৩৬) Which group of streptococcus is leading cause of neonatal sepsis?
Model Test 03.exp:
Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B Streptococcus, GBS) is a major and classic cause of neonatal sepsis, especially early-onset neonatal sepsis, which is usually acquired vertically from a colonized mother during labor or delivery.

  • S. agalactiae (GBS) → neonatal sepsis, pneumonia, meningitis

  • S. pyogenes (Group A) → pharyngitis, cellulitis, necrotizing fasciitis

  • Viridans streptococci → dental/oral flora, subacute endocarditis

  • Enterococcus faecalis → healthcare-associated UTI, biliary/intra-abdominal infections, endocarditis

High-yield Streptococcus recall:
Group B Strep = S. agalactiae = neonatal sepsis/meningitis.

Exam pearl:
“Newborn + sepsis = think Group B Streptococcus.”

Model Test 03.question: ৩৭) What is the percentage of water content in gallbladder bile?
Model Test 03.exp:
Gallbladder bile contains approximately 89% water. Compared with hepatic bile, gallbladder bile is more concentrated because the gallbladder absorbs water and electrolytes from stored bile.

  • Gallbladder bile → ~89% water

  • Hepatic bile → more dilute

  • Gallbladder concentration increases the relative concentration of bile salts, bilirubin, cholesterol, and other organic substances.

High-yield Bile recall:
Gallbladder → stores and concentrates bile by absorbing water and electrolytes.

Exam pearl:
“Gallbladder bile ≈ 89% water.”

Model Test 03.question: ৩৮) Which is a chronic complication of DM?
Model Test 03.exp:
Diabetic retinopathy is a chronic microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus caused by prolonged hyperglycemia and damage to retinal microvasculature.

  • Retinopathy → chronic microvascular complication

  • DKA → acute metabolic complication

  • HHS → acute metabolic complication

  • Hypoglycemia → acute complication, often treatment-related

Other important chronic complications include nephropathy, neuropathy, and macrovascular disease.

High-yield Diabetes recall:
Microvascular → Retinopathy + Nephropathy + Neuropathy
Macrovascular → CAD + Cerebrovascular disease + Peripheral arterial disease

Exam pearl:
“DM chronic microvascular complications = eye, kidney, nerve.”

Model Test 03.question: ৩৯) Which is the mediator of passive immunity?
Model Test 03.exp:
Passive immunity occurs when preformed antibodies are transferred to an individual rather than produced by their own immune system. Therefore, the mediator of passive immunity is antibody.

Examples:

  • Maternal IgG → fetus through placenta

  • Maternal IgA → infant through breast milk

  • Antiserum/immunoglobulin administration → artificial passive immunity

High-yield Immunology recall:
Passive immunity → antibodies transferred from another source → immediate protection, no long-term immune memory.

Exam pearl:
“Passive immunity = borrowed antibodies.”

Model Test 03.question: ৪০) Rhythm method of fertility control is based on the time of.....?
Model Test 03.exp:
The rhythm (calendar) method of fertility control is based on predicting the time of ovulation and avoiding intercourse during the fertile period surrounding ovulation.

Ovulation generally occurs about 14 days before the next menstrual period in a typical cycle. The fertile window accounts for the survival of sperm and the ovum.

High-yield Reproductive physiology recall:
Rhythm method → prediction of ovulation → avoidance of intercourse during fertile period.

Exam pearl:
“Rhythm method = ovulation-based fertility control.”

Model Test 03.question: ৪১) Intrinsic factor of Castle is secreted by which cell of small intestine?
Model Test 03.exp:
Intrinsic factor (Castle's factor) is secreted by parietal cells of the stomach, particularly in the fundus and body. It is essential for vitamin B12 absorption in the terminal ileum.

Therefore, the given options are technically incorrect:

  • Mucous cells → mucus

  • Argentaffin/enterochromaffin cells → various GI hormones/amines

  • Paneth cells → antimicrobial substances such as defensins and lysozyme

  • Goblet cells → mucus

  • Parietal cells → HCl + intrinsic factor

High-yield GI physiology recall:
Parietal cell → HCl + Intrinsic factor → B12 absorption in terminal ileum.

Exam pearl:
“Intrinsic factor = parietal cell, not small-intestinal cell.”

Model Test 03.question: ৪২) Which disinfectant of skin is used prior to venipuncture or immunization?
Model Test 03.exp:
70% ethanol (ethyl alcohol) is a commonly used skin antiseptic before procedures such as venipuncture and injections/immunization. It rapidly denatures microbial proteins and disrupts cell membranes.

  • 70% ethanol → commonly used for skin preparation

  • Chlorhexidine → widely used skin antiseptic, especially for surgical preparation

  • Iodophor → skin antiseptic/disinfectant

  • Thimerosal → preservative used in some pharmaceutical preparations; not the standard choice for routine venipuncture

High-yield Disinfection recall:
70% alcohol is more effective than absolute alcohol because water facilitates protein denaturation.

Exam pearl:
“For routine skin preparation before injection: 70% alcohol.”

Model Test 03.question: ৪৩) Depending upon the length of axon, neurons are divided into...... types?
Model Test 03.exp:
Based on the length of the axon, neurons are classically divided into two types:

  1. Golgi type I (projection neurons): Have a long axon that extends away from the cell body.

  2. Golgi type II (local circuit neurons): Have a short axon that remains near the cell body.

High-yield Neuroanatomy recall:
Golgi type I → long axon
Golgi type II → short axon

Exam pearl:
“Axon length classification = 2 types: Golgi I and Golgi II.”

Model Test 03.question: ৪৪) Bacterial flora of large intestine synthesizes all of the following except...?
Model Test 03.exp:
The normal gut flora of the large intestine synthesizes several vitamins, particularly vitamin K and some B vitamins. Vitamin E is not synthesized by intestinal bacteria.

  • Vitamin K → synthesized by gut bacteria

  • Folic acid (B9) → can be synthesized by some intestinal bacteria

  • Vitamin B12 → produced by certain bacteria, although human absorption from the colon is negligible

  • Vitamin E → not synthesized by gut flora

High-yield GI microbiology recall:
Gut flora → Vitamin K + some B vitamins
Vitamin E → dietary source, not a bacterial product

Exam pearl:
“Gut bacteria make K and some B vitamins, not vitamin E.”

Model Test 03.question: ৪৫) Which is not true about adjuvants?
Model Test 03.exp:
Adjuvants are substances added to an immunogen/vaccine to enhance the immune response. They generally do not become covalently attached to the immunogen.

  • Enhance immune response → True

  • Chemically unrelated to immunogen → Generally true

  • Differ from carrier protein → True

  • Covalently bound to immunogen → False

High-yield Immunology recall:
Adjuvant → enhances immunogenicity without itself being the antigen.
Examples: alum, Freund's adjuvant.

Exam pearl:
“Adjuvant boosts the immune response; it is not covalently bound to the immunogen.”

Model Test 03.question: ৪৬) Which glial cell provide myelination (insulation) around the nerve fibers in PNS?
Model Test 03.exp:
Schwann cells provide myelination (insulation) of nerve fibers in the peripheral nervous system (PNS). A single Schwann cell forms the myelin sheath around one segment (internode) of one axon.

  • Schwann cell → myelination in PNS

  • Oligodendrocyte → myelination in CNS

  • Satellite cell → supports neuronal cell bodies in PNS ganglia

  • Ependymal cells → line the ventricles and central canal

High-yield Neuroglia recall:
PNS → Schwann cell
CNS → Oligodendrocyte

Exam pearl:
“Schwann = PNS myelin; Oligodendrocyte = CNS myelin.”

Model Test 03.question: ৪৭) Hunger contractions are the movements of .......?
Model Test 03.exp:
Hunger contractions are strong rhythmic contractions of the empty stomach, especially when the stomach has been empty for several hours. They are part of the migrating motor complex (MMC) and contribute to the sensation of hunger.

  • Empty stomach → hunger contractions

  • Full stomach → mainly mixing and peristaltic contractions

  • Intestine → has its own motility patterns

High-yield GI physiology recall:
Hunger contractions → empty stomach → strong gastric contractions → sensation of hunger.

Exam pearl:
“Hunger = contractions of an empty stomach.”

Model Test 03.question: ৪৮) Ruffini end organ is a cutaneous receptor for......?
Model Test 03.exp:
Ruffini endings (Ruffini corpuscles) are slowly adapting receptors associated with skin stretch and are classically considered warmth receptors in basic physiology MCQs.

  • Ruffini ending → warmth + skin stretch

  • Meissner corpuscle → fine/light touch

  • Pacinian corpuscle → vibration + deep pressure

  • Cold receptors → mainly free nerve endings

High-yield Sensory receptor recall:
Warmth → Ruffini
Cold → Free nerve endings
Vibration → Pacinian
Fine touch → Meissner

Exam pearl:
“Ruffini = warmth.”

Model Test 03.question: ৪৯) What type of necrosis occurs in TB?
Model Test 03.exp:
Tuberculosis (TB) classically produces caseous necrosis, a form of necrosis characterized by a soft, cheese-like appearance. It occurs within tuberculous granulomas due to the chronic immune response to Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

  • TB → Caseous necrosis

  • Coagulative → commonly seen in ischemic infarction of solid organs

  • Liquefactive → brain infarction, abscesses

  • Suppurative → pus-forming bacterial infections

High-yield Pathology recall:
TB → caseous necrosis + granuloma
Myocardial infarction → coagulative necrosis
Brain infarction → liquefactive necrosis

Exam pearl:
“TB = cheese-like caseation.”

Model Test 03.question: ৫০) Which is used for sterilization of endoscopes?
Model Test 03.exp:
Glutaraldehyde is a high-level disinfectant/chemical sterilant traditionally used for heat-sensitive medical equipment, including endoscopes, because it can achieve sterilization with appropriate concentration and exposure time.

  • Glutaraldehyde → endoscopes and other heat-sensitive instruments

  • Hydrogen peroxide → also used for high-level disinfection/sterilization in some systems

  • Phenols → mainly surface disinfectants

  • Detergents → cleaning agents, not sterilizing agents

High-yield Sterilization recall:
Heat-sensitive instruments → chemical sterilants such as glutaraldehyde.

Exam pearl:
“Endoscope = Glutaraldehyde.”
